instructions: Answer the questions below. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
word_limit: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER

items.prompt: Sound can be measured; what does the lecturer say noise is instead?
items.explanation: Sound is a physical event that can be measured; noise, on the other hand, is a judgement — sound that someone does not want. That is why two people hearing the same level can be bothered to different degrees.

items.prompt: If the amount of traffic on a road doubles, by how many decibels does the level go up?
items.explanation: Because the scale is logarithmic, doubling the traffic adds three decibels, not ten; this is close to the smallest change most people can notice.

items.prompt: Which part of the frequency range does the weighting used for environmental work play down?
items.evidence: the weighting used for environmental work discounts the low end heavily
items.explanation: Because the ear is much less sensitive to low frequencies, the measuring device applies a weighting and largely discounts sounds at the low end.

items.prompt: How often does a large built-up area have to renew its strategic noise map?
items.explanation: The three-year figure in old textbooks is no longer valid; the map is renewed every five years.

items.prompt: According to the more recent figures, what share of the exposed population is affected by road traffic?
items.evidence: the more recent figures put it nearer four fifths
items.explanation: The proportion once given as two thirds is now nearer four fifths in the new figures; rail comes second and air comes third.
